title: Zero or more arguments with varargs

blocks.text: A varargs parameter, written `int... numbers`, accepts any number of arguments, none included, and the method sees them as an array. It must be the last parameter, so a method that needs at least one value takes that one first: `max(int first, int... rest)`.

items: `sum(int... numbers)` returns the total: `sum(1, 2, 3)` is `6`, `sum(10, 20)` is `30`, and `sum()` is `0`. An explicit `null` array counts as no numbers: `sum((int[]) null)` is `0`.
`max(int first, int... rest)` returns the largest of all its arguments: `max(3, 9, 4)` is `9`, `max(5)` is `5`, and `max(-2, -7)` is `-2`.

cases.says: max(5) is 5 and max(9, 3, 4) is 9: first is one of the values.

concepts: A varargs parameter accepts zero or more arguments as an array, and must be the method's last parameter.
